newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA looks to diversify in NZ, Asia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA looks to diversify in NZ, Asia.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia managing director David Murray said on Thursday the bank wanted to diversity its interests in New Zealand and in Asia.

"We'd be looking to do more over there," Murray told a Securities Institute of Australia function, referring to the bank's New Zealand unit ASB Bank. "We're looking to diversification there (New Zealand) and in Asia," he said.
Murray later said CBA had been successful in New Zealand with ASB Bank, but that it still had only a relatively small presence.

"So if we had any opportunities to expand any further, we'd like to take them, because we know the market and we think we could provide a pretty good service there," Murray told reporters after the Securities Institute address.
Murray agreed that the only large bank in New Zealand not already owned by CBA or its Australian competitors was the National Bank of New Zealand Ltd, which is owned by Lloyds TSB Group Plc.
"For that reason, we'd consider both acquisition opportunities and more rapid internal development opportunities, because we can't get caught with limited bargaining power," he said.
"We keep an eye on everything all the time," he said when asked if CBA had specifically looked at National Bank of New Zealand.
Murray also later detailed CBA's new push into Asia.
He said the bank had decided to expand its Asian activities and would seek out new joint ventures in Indonesia, China, Vietnam and India.
